newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-HANSA SAYS MERITA BONDS WILL BE 2-YR BENCHMARK.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-HANSA SAYS MERITA BONDS WILL BE 2-YR BENCHMARK.

text.p: Hansabank-Latvija, part of Estonia's Hansapank, said on Wednesday that the lat-denominated bonds issued by Finnish Merita Bank would become a benchmark for the Latvian debt market.

"The bonds will serve as a benchmark for two-year Latvian financial markets, for the interbank market," Maris Vinklers of Hansabank-Latvija's financial markets unit, the co-leader of the issue, told Reuters.
"They will also be a benchmark for Latvian government two-year T-bills expected to be issued in the coming two weeks, because the risks are pretty similar," Vinklers said.
The finance ministry has already said it would issue two-year T-bills in April.
Both short term and long term interest rates could be affected by Merita bonds by reducing the quantity of lats in circulation, he said.
"We expect in the coming months some corparate lat bonds and commercial papers of both Latvian and foreign companies, which could also be affected," Vinklers said.
A Latvian commercial bank foreign exchange dealer said the nine percent coupon is quite favourable compared to the deposit and equities market.
"Theoretically we could see a rise in interest rates, because 15 milllion lats is big money for Latvia," he added.
